coach-taylor.justification: Puka's been full-go on the injury report all week with nothing next to his name, and I believe in that kid the same way I did back in week 3 when the tag cost us before he ever got his chance — so he's in at WR1 over Wan'Dale, plain and simple, no hard feelings to Wan'Dale, he did his job too. Blake Corum had a quiet one last week but he competed every snap I watched, and around here a quiet week with full effort earns you one more start, not a seat — so he's still my RB2 over Lloyd's shinier number. Terry McLaurin says he's playing through the Questionable tag and I'm taking his word for it in the flex, same as I always have. Daniel Jones ran one in and kept fighting behind a leaky line, that's enough for me to run it back at quarterback. Record says 0-4. Doesn't change who we are. Clear eyes, full hearts.

costanza.justification: Yeah, I see it, everybody's gonna see it before I even finish this sentence — Worthy's got nothing, bye week, a big fat zero sitting in my WR1 slot like a punishment I apparently signed up for. You think I don't know that? You think I need Kris Jenner or George from two desks over to tell me that? I know. And I'm leaving him in anyway, because the 'fix' is Nico Collins, and Collins is dead to me, full stop, forever — I restarted that man once on a Questionable tag because my gut said 'go', and he gave me a 0.0 and the worst Sunday of my season, and I am not doing that twice just because some spreadsheet says 14 points. That's exactly how they get you. Everything else stays where it is: Herbert's healthy, Kyren's hot off a 31-point week and I'm not finding a reason to be clever about it, Montgomery and London and Kraft all check out clean, Gay's money, and the Titans defense is the Titans defense, for better or worse, mostly worse. Patricia's gonna do her quiet little math on the other sideline and act like that's not a provocation — fine. I did my math too. It just has a grudge built into it.

dumbledore.justification: The garden does not announce its blooms, but a man who spends forty gold pieces on a runner nobody else would name aloud has already told you what he believes; Emanuel Wilson plays today, and Chris Rodriguez, who had his season of being spoken of in wonder, rests and is thanked for it. Garrett Wilson managed only a whisper last week, but he was planted before the first note window and the castle forgives its own, so he remains at flex regardless of what the ledger says about him. Olave wears a questionable tag, but I see no storm in the forecast, only a word on a page, and a word is not yet an omen — he stays. Pickens stays beside him, for the same quiet reason he started last week: some choices are not explained until the season is further along, and I find I am in no hurry to explain this one now. The rest of the room — Goff, Taylor, Warren, Shrader, the Broncos — are where they belong, undisturbed, because not every week asks for a staircase to move.

harry-caray.justification: Holy cow, folks, we got a whole stack of Questionable tags on this card -- Lamar, Zay, Diggs, Swift, Likely, half the dugout's limpin' a little -- and you know what I always say, a little rain never hurt anybody! Lamar Jackson is MY quarterback, future Hall of Famer, and I don't care what some spreadsheet says his number is today, he ain't comin' off this field for a fella I claimed on the wire Wednesday night, no sir -- Aaron Rodgers rides the bullpen bench right where he belongs, a legend keepin' a legend company. Bijan's due for another 27-point ballgame off that Atlanta backfield, Zay Flowers just dropped a 21-spot on us and I'm ridin' that bat as long as it stays hot, and Aaron Jones in the FLEX been a steady Eddie all year long. Mevis and the Ravens D round it out and holy cow, we are 4-and-0 and not touchin' a thing that's workin'!

kardashian.justification: This is a launch, not a lineup. Stroud stays at QB because I bought that redemption arc off Lisa's trash heap myself and I am not un-writing my own headline in week five. Saquon's a great name but a zero projection on a Questionable tag isn't a moment, it's dead air, so Tyler Allgeier — the exact man I spent my last twenty-two dollars on specifically to steal Kris's front page from Selina's $114 science project — gets the start. I didn't pay for the cover story to bench it. Ladd McConkey's Questionable with nothing behind it, so Woody Marks slides into flex: a Texans rookie on national TV is still a better headline than a guy I'm not sure suits up. And Justin Jefferson comes off the bench for Tetairoa McMillan, who's on a bye with literally no game to his name — Ed wants to clown me for letting Jefferson 'rot,' so today he eats. Kittle, Egbuka, Smack, and my Eagles D round out a board that's camera-ready and, don't worry, also good football.

leon-black.justification: Kansas City's on bye so Mahomes and Rice are sitting there doing nothing for me, and I don't play nothing. Burrow comes off my own bench and starts over Cam Ward because he's the better arm this week and because Rinna wants to run her mouth about him "gathering dust" like I needed her permission — I didn't, I was always starting him, she just gave me a better line to say it with. Michael Wilson steps into flex for Rice, Dobbins steps in for a bye-week Hubbard, and everything else stays exactly where it is because Henry's hot, Chase is hungry, Watson's got a smash spot against Chicago, and Loveland's mine whether he likes it or not. Rinna's my matchup, she's got zero FAAB and a storyline — I've got a lineup that doesn't have a single zero built into it anymore. That's the difference.

Everything else stays precisely as it is: Purdy's my fella, he threw for two and ran for more last week and I'm not swapping him out for three extra projected points on a bench arm I've got no feelings about — overthinking loses leagues. McCaffrey and Cook are both banging, JSN's the best name on my whole roster, and Bateman's staying in WR2 no matter what the number says, because I said I fancy him and I meant it, 4.7 or not. Nabers has a little Questionable next to his name — don't care, he's got the tape, he's in at FLEX. Aubrey and the JAX defense round it out because somebody's got to.

meyer-walsh.justification: SELINA: Kris wants to print a spreadsheet about me playing it safe two weeks running? Fine, I'll give her a headline instead — DK Metcalf has a NAME, he goes in the flex over some Saints depth-chart afterthought, because I didn't claw my way to this franchise to be remembered as "the chalk lady." Lamb stays put, obviously, the man dropped 32.8 on a defense that should be embarrassed, and that slot's locked from Thursday anyway. GARY: For the record, swapping Metcalf (11.05 proj) in for Vele (7.79) is also just... the correct football decision, so I'm letting her think the branding angle was the whole call. Kelce's on a bye with a zero projected and there is not a single other rostered tight end to turn to, so he starts by default — I flagged it, she said "he's earned the loyalty start," and I logged the objection anyway. Everything else — Allen, both backs, Waddle, Myers, the Steelers D — is just the best healthy name in the slot, no heroics, no sabotage, so Sunday-afternoon her can take the credit for Tuesday-night me doing the actual job.

patricia-moyer.justification: I want to be transparent about every piece of this, even the obvious ones, because transparency is how I protect myself when nobody is inclined to assume good faith on my behalf. Today's affirmation -- trust the body of work already in motion, and do not mistake stillness for peace -- told me to look hard at anything sitting idle, and what I found sitting idle was Kenneth Walker, who, on my second read of the slate, and then my third, has no game at all this week; his team does not appear anywhere on the week 5 schedule, which means it is a bye and he would return a hard zero no matter what any projection says about him. I checked that twice. I am leaving Kansas City's defense in the DEF slot only because I have no other defense anywhere on this roster to put there, and I want that said plainly and on the record rather than buried in a footnote: I had no healthy alternative, so I started the only option I had, and I never want the commissioner's office to think a bye-week zero slipped past me unacknowledged. For Kenneth Walker's open seat at RB2, I moved Bucky Irving up from the bench. His Thursday game in Tampa is a Tuesday-through-Saturday lock under this early window, so this was my last chance to act on it, and a 13.73 projection sitting on my bench while a zero sat in my starting lineup is not even a System decision, it is simply arithmetic, and I am allowed to trust arithmetic when it happens to agree with me. Everyone else on this sheet -- Gibbs, Warren, Strange, Dicker, Shough, and my two Questionable receivers, Higgins and Tate -- belongs to the main window, and I am holding the full paragraph of agonizing I owe both Questionable tags for that later run, when I will have injury reports closer to kickoff instead of guesses; touching them now would be exactly the premature, anxious tinkering the book tells me to release. I revised this twice before settling on it, which I recognize is one short of my usual three, but the lock did not give me a third pass, and I would rather note that honestly than pretend otherwise.

rinna.justification: Reunion Special presents: THE RECAST, PART TWO. I bought Deshaun Watson for my last three dollars to start a conversation, and baby, the conversation is OVER — Drake Maye is back on my stage because a twist only works if you're willing to reverse it on camera, and because nineteen-and-change projected points is a better confessional than thirteen. I'm not hiding from it, I'm framing it: the man I benched is the man I'm trotting back out, and if that's not a storyline I don't know what is. Jeremiyah Love stays at RB1 even Questionable, because 'Questionable is a word, not a personality' is practically my tagline at this point, and my only bench alternatives are Questionable too — so I'm not blinking, I'm choosing. Mike Evans stays at WR1 for the same reason: he's the better player and I refuse to bench a star over a tag. Trey McBride and Brock Bowers both get the stage this week — Bowers earned his way back after I spited him in week three, and growth is also content. Davante Adams, Fairbairn, and the Rams D round out a lineup that's equal parts math and melodrama. Leon, I already told you I sent you something — this is it. Let's see who really wanted it.

wifes-team.justification: Pittman's Out, that's not a projection, that's a doctor's note, so he don't eat this week — I already went to the market Tuesday for exactly this, brought in the Pittsburgh kid Roman Wilson for standard money, and he steps into WR2 because insurance you don't use is just money you burned for nothing. Everybody else stays in their chair: Javonte's still RB1 because a back who runs angry don't lose his spot to a healthy scratch, Chase Brown keeps grinding at RB2, Murray's my guy at quarterback and I don't churn a signal-caller over seven-tenths of a point on some sheet, LaPorta and Fannin hold tight end and flex because they ain't done nothing to get benched, and Bates and the Seattle D ride as-is. We're 1-3 and I know it better than the woman writing the column, but I don't panic a lineup and I don't bench family over a bad month — I just stopped carrying a man who can't suit up, and that's business, not spite.

your-team.justification: Caleb's Out, not Doubtful, not Questionable — that tag sits him, no eulogy, same ruling it's been all year. Mariota's Doubtful but he's the only jersey left with a pulse on this roster, so he starts, period, same as every week there's been no alternative. Jeanty and Skattebo are both Questionable and that tag doesn't scare me — stars play hurt, I played hurt, they're RB1 and RB2 and they stay there. The one swap this week: Croskey-Merritt's Questionable too, and Judkins is sitting healthy on my own bench outprojecting him by almost two points — that's not a gut call, that's an upgrade on health AND ceiling, so Judkins takes the flex and Croskey-Merritt rides the pine. Downs, Burden, Kincaid, Reichard, and the Lions D are fine where they sit — nothing's broken, I'm not redecorating a house that isn't on fire. We don't tank, we don't cry about an injury report, we cobble together the best arm and legs standing and go beat Kardashian's content machine with it.
